title: From critical crossings to quenched near-critical universality in Voronoi percolation
coverage:
I read the full text of Sections 1, 5 (site expansion), 6 (sewing/replacement) and 7 (identification and the quenched limit). In Section 2 I read the arm inputs, pivotal-arm and localization lemmas, quenched Cardy, good sequences and the pivotal-scale lemma. I read Section 3 up to the stopped-target-face lemma and the first part of Section 4 (boundary-pairing readout and the start of forced-square continuity).

Checks I did by hand:
- The exact history law: U uniform gives P0 + q_e w_t, with masses min t_i at all-ones and -max t_i at all-zeros.
- The Mecke/factorial-moment expansion, and that the extra q_e factor kills repeated replica labels.
- The merging-forest bound: at most 2k lives; probe disjointness, both nested and incomparable; telescoping gives one inverse p(l_f) per accepted edge; the diameter charge is at most k; A(l,L)^{-1} <= C l^{-g}.
- The factorial integration: k^{gk/2} * sum_j binom((k+J)^2, j) k^{-j} / k! <= C^k k^{-(1-g/2)k}.
- The L^p cutoff with gp < 2.
- The triangular pivotal upper bound: the dyadic (u,d) sum gives m a u^{2-g}.
- The Efron-Stein corner sum in quenched Cardy: (s/u)^{2a} u^{2b0}.
- The necklace five-arm exclusion argument (hex duality in each gap).
- The signed bit factorization a_A a_B (a constant response is killed by the centered weight).
- The adaptive exchange: a measure-preserving involution, and trial status is invariant.
- The n-trial averaging bound rho + C*C/n.
- Calibration: |1 - c* J| <= z gives a unique c > 0, then B > 0 and r_e = q_e/(B + o(1)).
- The CDF/threshold identity under the closed mark rule, and the L^2 concentration from two replicas.

Not checked line by line: the remaining SLE6 exploration and loop-convergence topology in Section 3, the later forced-square witness arguments in Section 4, and the boundary-arm bootstrap lemmas in Section 2.
main_claim: Assume the annealed scalar Cardy formula for Poisson-Voronoi percolation. Then the threshold vectors of all rational polygonal quads under the monotone coupling, each model normalized by its own mean number of color-pivotal sites for the unit square, converge on the triangular lattice to a law nu_triangle. For Voronoi, the law conditional on the tessellation converges in probability (bounded-Lipschitz metric) to the same nu_triangle.
sibling_notes: The family-224 board had one sibling entry: rank 39, 'A Pivotal Amplitude for Voronoi Percolation from Cardy's Formula', reported no_gap_found. This paper does not depend on that sibling's amplitude. It explicitly avoids assuming convergence of a microscopic pivotal amplitude and calibrates c_e through the Q0 first coefficient (exactly 1). There is no circularity. Its only external input is the companion's scalar annealed Cardy theorem (Hypothesis 1.1). The board entry did not change my analysis.
